failed_or_weak: r4-wind-001 was rejected (cap $10 below the H100 rate x (max_hours + 0.25)); resubmitted unchanged as r4-wind-002 with cap $12
patchnet+u (wind channels appended, input-aware linear baseline) generalises worse than the blind patchnet; slotnet+u helps only at h <= 4. The input-aware nets are a first design, not a ceiling

GPU float64 runs are not deterministic: on the H100 two copies of one state with one key in one vmap call differ by 1.2e-7 in level 1 after 3 ticks, and two separately compiled lax.map runners of the same law differ by 6e-13 after 1 tick [runner_check]; the vmap runner agrees with lax.map at that floor (4e-13), as on the CPU (6e-14). CRN pairs (MW, twins) therefore decorrelate after about 5 ticks; the estimators stay unbiased but noisier, and per-item CRN effects are noisy, so the objects ideal-loss z (squared error) is a lower bound
the identity-event split is informative only at h <= 4
next_steps: input-aware coarse predictor that cannot lose to the blind one: patchnet plus the +u2 response fitted on patchnet's own residuals, and input dropout for the wind channels; one more GPU job of about 0.5 h ($2-3), CPU-minutes of code

B3 for the exam: an input-aware predictor trained on simulations (simulate-to-train, as in round4/sbi) in place of level-1 data, to make 'actions matter' pass in the coarse view; size it from the ideal contrast here (coarse ES z 7.6-8.4 at 64 items)
